claims.text: Hybrid machine-learning-informed thermodynamic integration can compute both solid and liquid free energies for multicomponent high-entropy alloys.
The proposed workflow retains vibrational entropy, anharmonicity, and electron–phonon effects.
The method will cost substantially less than both direct ab initio molecular dynamics and TOR-TILD for alloys containing at least four elements.
The method can maintain free-energy accuracy within a few meV/atom of explicit ab initio benchmarks.
Al-Cr-Co-Fe-Ni is a representative material system for testing interatomic-potential methods in a quinary high-entropy alloy.
A machine-learning interatomic potential should be trained on limited, targeted ab initio molecular-dynamics data.
The trained potential should be coupled to accelerated thermodynamic integration to predict solid and liquid free energies, melting temperatures, and heat capacities.
Sampling from approximately 0.5 to 1.1 times the melting temperature will include the stable solid phase or phases and the fluid state.
Short ab initio molecular-dynamics simulations can seed a training set that captures relevant short-range order and fluctuating local structures near the solid–liquid transition.
Interatomic-potential simulations can reproduce first-principles structural properties and high-temperature short-range ordering in Al-Cr-Co-Fe-Ni.
Accurate force prediction over relevant configurations permits low-cost thermodynamic integration over the required phase space.
Thermodynamic integration driven by the proposed machine-learning potential can incorporate vibrational entropy and anharmonic free-energy contributions.
Thermodynamic integration driven by the proposed machine-learning potential can incorporate electron–phonon coupling.
The proposed workflow mimics ab initio sampling at a fraction of the computational expense.
The workflow will reduce computational time by an order of magnitude relative to explicit ab initio molecular dynamics and TOR-TILD.
The resulting melting temperatures and high-temperature thermodynamic properties will be comparable to those from explicit ab initio workflows.
Established elemental or binary free-energy benchmarks validated against experiment provide the proposed baseline.
The method is applicable to alloys containing four or five principal elements from room temperature to slightly above melting.
Systems with strong chemical short-range order or more than five principal elements may require additional model refinement.
A deviation greater than approximately 5 meV/atom in free energy, greater than 5% in melting temperature, or computational cost comparable to or exceeding TOR-TILD would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The primary test range begins at approximately 0.5 Tmelt, whereas the stated applicability boundary begins at room temperature; the hypothesis does not explain how fidelity below 0.5 Tmelt would be established.
